channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: FlyDubai attacker intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, investigation finds
item.description: The ongoing investigation has found the attacker intended to crash the plane into Israel's Ben Gurion International Airport, a person familiar with the matter but not authorized to speak publicly told NPR.

item.title: Retired FBI special agent discusses the FlyDubai attack investigation
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with retired FBI special agent Lara Burns about the investigation into the FlyDubai attack and the lessons for law enforcement agencies worldwide.

item.title: U.S. Marine suspected in woman's death arrested in Japan
item.description: A U.S. Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder in Okinawa, prompting renewed Japanese criticism of the conduct of American military personnel.
item.content:encoded: A U.S. Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder in Okinawa, prompting renewed Japanese criticism of the conduct of American military personnel.

item.title: Supreme Court's new term kicks off with blockbuster climate change case
item.description: The case centers on whether local governments can hold giant energy companies accountable for the local harms of climate change, but it has repercussions beyond climate.

item.title: From floating saunas to clinical trials: How heat might help mental health
item.description: While scientists have a decent understanding of how sauna and other forms of heat exposure exercises our cardiovascular system, they know relatively little about its impact on mental health.

item.title: Mahmoud Khalil's memoir is a peek inside immigration detention and his fight to stay
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Mahmoud Khalil, who was arrested at Columbia University by immigration authorities last year. His memoir is "No Land to Stand On: Notes From Detention."

item.title: Texas Senate race shatters state's campaign spending record
item.description: Combined spending on advertising by Democratic state Rep. James Talarico, Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, and super PACs supporting each of them has already topped $240 million.

item.title: In Virginia, voting rights restoration is tough. A ballot measure could change that
item.description: Virginia has been one of the toughest places for someone convicted of a felony to get their voting rights back. An amendment to the state constitution -- on November's ballot -- would change that.
item.content:encoded: Virginia has been one of the toughest places for someone convicted of a felony to get their voting rights back. An amendment to the state constitution -- on November's ballot -- would change that.

item.title: Iraq's Iranian-backed militias say it'll cease attacks once U.S. military withdraws
item.description: Iraq's main Iranian-backed militias say they will stop attacks after the U.S. military's withdrawal from the country.
